title: Part Time Bookkeeper
description:
Part-Time Bookkeeper

Rural Location Part-Time Immediate Start Available

Are you an experienced Bookkeeper looking for a flexible part-time role in a friendly, down-to-earth business?

We're seeking a proactive and organised individual to join our client in a beautiful rural setting. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys variety in their day, takes pride in keeping the finances in order, and isn't afraid to roll their sleeves up and help wherever needed.

The Role
You'll be responsible for supporting the day-to-day financial administration of the business, including:
- Managing bookkeeping activities using Xero
- Processing invoices and payments
- Bank reconciliations
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns
- Maintaining accurate financial records
- Supporting the wider team with general administrative duties as required
- Assisting with a variety of tasks in a small business environment

About You
We're looking for someone who:
- Has proven bookkeeping experience
- Is confident using Xero
- Has experience preparing VAT returns
- Has excellent attention to detail
- Is organised, reliable and self-motivated
- Enjoys working as part of a small, supportive team
- Has a flexible attitude and is happy to muck in with a range of duties

What's on Offer?

Flexible part-time hours
Friendly and supportive working environment
Beautiful rural location
Varied role with plenty of autonomy
Dog-friendly workplace, because we know our four-legged friends can make the working day even better!

If you're looking for a role where your experience will be valued and you'll genuinely feel part of the team, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply or find out more, please get in touch today.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll & People Administrator

Redditch Part-Time, Permanent (22.5 Hours per Week)

Are you an organised administrator with excellent attention to detail and a passion for supporting people?

An established employer is looking to appoint a Payroll & People Administrator to support their payroll and people function. Reporting to the Head of Finance, you'll play a key role in supporting payroll administration and employee records management across sites. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, thrives on organisation, and takes pride in delivering first-class administrative support.

The Role

As Payroll & People Administrator, you will provide essential support to the Payroll Manager and wider People team, ensuring payroll information is accurate, employee records are maintained, and team member queries are handled professionally and efficiently.

Key Responsibilities
- Responding to payroll and people-related queries from employees and managers
- Supporting the Payroll Manager with payroll preparation and administration
- Gathering and checking timesheets, absence records, overtime, and pay amendments
- Processing new starter, leaver, and contractual change documentation
- Maintaining accurate employee records and electronic filing systems
- Preparing letters, forms, contracts, and other employee documentation
- Handling confidential and sensitive information with discretion
- Providing general administrative support to the Payroll and People functions

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail
- Confidence communicating via telephone and email
- The ability to manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and priorities
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly in Excel and Outlook
- A professional and confidential approach when dealing with sensitive information
- A positive, proactive, and team-focused attitude

Desirable Experience
- Previous experience within Payroll, HR, Recruitment, or Administrative roles
- Understanding of payroll processes and employee administration

Training can be provided for the right candidate, making this a fantastic opportunity for someone looking to develop their career within payroll and people administration.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary dependent on experience
- Part-time working hours (22.5 hours per week)
- Company pension scheme
- Employee benefits programme
- Ongoing training and development opportunities
- Flexible working pattern
- Casual dress
- Free onsite parking

Apply Today

If you're a highly organised and people-focused administrator looking for a varied role within a growing organisation, we'd love to hear from you.

This is a permanent, part-time position based in Redditch, offering 20 hours per week and a competitive salary dependent on experience.

For more information on this position, please contact James Randall at Four Squared Recruitment.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller
Pershore
Full-time - permanent
£30,000p/a - £35,000p/a

Job Summary
We are seeking a diligent and detail-oriented Credit Controller to join our clients finance team. The Credit Controller will play an essential role in managing and maintaining the company's credit and collections processes, ensuring timely payments, minimising overdue balances, and fostering strong relationships with clients.
This role is essential to maintaining healthy cash flow for the business.
The successful candidate will have previous accounting or finance experience, enabling them to identify discrepancies, investigate account issues, recognise potential risks, and proactively resolve problems before they impact the business.

Key Responsibilities
Credit Management
- Establish and maintain strong internal and external relationships to ensure effective credit management.
- Strong organisation and co-ordination skills ensuring agreed timelines are met.
- Excellent communication skills for dealing with internal and external partners.
- Ability to work across various platforms and systems.
- Reporting to management team on all client accounts.
- Providing insights and recommendations on improving collections processes.
- Reviewing account activity and financial data to identify trends, anomalies, or potential payment issues.
- Investigating and resolving account discrepancies in collaboration with customers and internal stakeholders.

Key Skills and Competencies
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent communication and negotiation abilities.
- High level of attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in various software systems.
- Ability to work independently and meet deadlines under pressure.
- Knowledge of credit control practices and financial regulations.
- Previous accounting or finance experience with the ability to analyse account information, identify discrepancies, and proactively resolve issues.
- A sound understanding of accounting principles and the impact of credit control on overall business cash flow and financial performance.

This is a full time permanent position with a salary of £30,000 - £35,000p/a.

For more information on this position please contact Harriet at Four Squared Recruitment.

If you have not heard from us within three weeks of submitting your application, please assume that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion. We thank you for your interest and encourage you to apply for future opportunities.

title: Onboarding Coordinator
description:
The Onboarding Coordinator sits within the Operations Team and plays a key role in ensuring a positive onboarding experience for learners and clients. The successful candidate will support the delivery of efficient, compliant and process-driven learner onboarding activities, helping to maximise apprenticeship starts and maintain high levels of client satisfaction.

This role requires excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. The Onboarding Coordinator will work closely with colleagues across Client Success, Compliance and Operations to ensure all learners are onboarded accurately and in line with current DfE Funding Rules.

Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate and support the end-to-end learner onboarding process, ensuring all onboarding activities are completed accurately and within agreed timescales.
- Complete process-driven onboarding tasks, maintaining accurate learner records, documentation and system updates throughout the onboarding journey.
- Track and monitor upcoming apprenticeship start dates, learner volumes and onboarding progress to support the achievement of monthly start targets.
- Liaise with learners, employers and internal teams to ensure all onboarding requirements are completed and any issues are resolved promptly.
- Work collaboratively with the Client Success Team to support client queries relating to learner onboarding.
- Monitor work-in-progress activities and proactively follow up on outstanding documentation and onboarding requirements to support timely learner starts.
- Update clients on apprentice onboarding progress, upcoming starts and learners approaching programme completion and highlighting any required actions.
- Maintain Apprenticeship Service Account records, ensuring apprentices are correctly uploaded and funding requirements are met.
- Work closely with the Compliance Team to ensure all onboarding documentation is complete, accurate and compliant with DfE Funding Rules and internal policies.
- Prepare internal communications and updates regarding onboarding progress, apprentice approvals, upcoming starts and operational activity.
- Identify opportunities for continuous improvement within onboarding processes, systems and client experience.
- Complete all mandatory training and Continuing Professional Development (CPD) activities in a timely manner and actively seek opportunities for personal development.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise
- Experience or understanding of Learning & Development, ideally within a FE & Skills provider, with experience and knowledge of the English Apprenticeship Levy
- Experience of Onboarding learners to Apprenticeship programmes in line with DfE Funding Rules
- Understanding of vocational qualifications including Apprenticeships and Functional Skills
- Experience of working within a regulatory environment
- Experience of working positively both within a team and independently
- Experience of working remotely and self-motivating time management
- Experience working with databases/platforms (Desirable - experience of using Aptem)
- Good analytical abilities and able to be decisive
- An ability to analyse a situation with employers or Apprentices and adapt the communication accordingly, to offer appropriate information, advice, support and guidance
- Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills, with confidence to deal with senior stakeholders
- Excellent IT skills, including all Microsoft office packages
- Ability to maintain discretion and confidentiality at all times
- Experience of working in client facing environments or high internal customer care departments with a positive service approach
- Self-motivated, process-driven, organised with strong attention to detail and ability to manage own workload and meet deadlines
- An understanding of Insurance and Financial Service industry including clients and professional bodies (Desirable)

title: Group HR Co-ordinator
company: James Andrew Recruitment Solutions (JAR Solutions) - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are pleased to be supporting our client in their search for a HR Co-ordinator who can provide comprehensive recruitment administration support as part of its busy HR team. This permanent role is based in Redditch, offers hybrid working with 3 days from home, and pays up to £30,000 per annum.

You will deliver a first-class HR administration service across the full recruitment process, acting as a key point of contact for approved vacancies and helping to ensure a positive experience for candidates, hiring managers and wider stakeholders.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Co-ordinating the end-to-end recruitment process for approved vacancies, supporting hiring managers and candidates throughout
- Facilitating candidate selection and interview activity in partnership with hiring managers and the wider HR team
- Developing and posting job adverts through the applicant tracking system
- Maintaining and updating the ATS platform, recruitment records and associated software
- Managing the careers inbox, responding to queries and escalating matters where appropriate
- Completing candidate screening, pre-employment checks and right-to-work documentation
- Supporting onboarding activity for new joiners and helping the HR team provide a seamless early employment experience
- Producing standard resourcing reports and maintaining accurate recruitment data for wider reporting and analytics
- Contributing to wider HR activity, projects and continuous improvement across processes and systems

Experience required:
- Proven administration experience, ideally gained within HR, recruitment or a busy people-focused function
- A customer-focused approach, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally with candidates and internal stakeholders
- Strong attention to detail and excellent written communication skills
- Good IT skills, including confidence using Excel and producing or maintaining reports
- A flexible and adaptable approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and work at pace
- An inquisitive, creative and improvement-focused mindset
- Experience using HR systems or applicant tracking systems would be beneficial

James Andrews are acting as an employment agency and business in relation to this role.

We aim to respond to all applications personally; however, due to the volume of applications this is not always possible. If you have not heard from us within 72 hours, please assume that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Administrator
company: Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
advertiser_name: Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
description: Due to the transformation of our services, we are recruiting for an enthusiastic and proactive administrator to join and enhance our children's therapy team, providing outstanding care for patients across Worcestershire. A willingness to learn and expand your skills will be positively encouraged and we will provide you with resources to develop and progress a long-term career. This is an administrator post supporting in various aspects of admin such The team are countywide with bases in Kidderminster, Redditch, Bromsgrove and Worcester. Applicants must read the attached guidance notes before submitting your application for full understanding of Trust requirements. The successful candidate will need to have significant proven experience working within a busy team, demonstrate a flexible approach, and have the ability to stay calm and always work professionally. As a highly organised individual you will need the ability to prioritise and organise work so that tasks are completed in a timely manner following agreed processes and always have the best interest of the patient at the centre of everything you do. You also need to be willing to work with senior management to improve and support the implementation of change when needed. It is essential that you are proficient in IT skills including knowledge of the Microsoft Office Packages along with excellent communication and interpersonal skills. You will be answering the phone and taking messages, dealing with patient appointments, arranging and booking clinics, general admin duties which include photocopying, filing, diary management. You may be asked to cover at another base occasionally to cover for leave or absence. You will also be trained to do administration tasks for both Paediatric Occupational Therapy and Physiotherapy teams. For full details of the duties and criteria for the role please refer to the job description and person specification attached.
